newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Credit Suisse starts Internet banking.
newsitem.headline: Credit Suisse starts Internet banking.

text.p: Credit Suisse Group said it would become the first Swiss bank to offer Internet banking from April 14.

"From April 14, 1997, Credit Suisse customers will be able to carry out payment transactions, account transfers, securities orders and other banking busines via the Internet," it said in a statement issued before a news conference.

A Credit Suisse statement said all customer data would be protected by a multi-tier security system and in particular by a 128-bit encryption software called SecureNet offered by the Swiss network services company Swiss Online AG.
Credit Suisse is the Swiss banking arm of the Credit Suisse Group that also includes Credit Suisse First Boston.
SecureNet was developed by a Swiss company, r3security engineering ag, the Swiss SonntagsZeitung newspaper reported.
"The technological breakthrough by the Credit Suisse Group has an effect on the entire Swiss business world," the paper said in its weekend edition.

By finding a secure enough programm to protect financial data on the public internet, Credit Suisse was effectively opening the internet to other lucrative commercial uses that have been stalled so far by worries about the safety of money and information, SonntagsZeitung said.
Retail bank services are already available electronically for customers at Credit Suisse and most other Swiss banks, but they use an older technology hooked into the cable television network.

SontagsZeitungs aid the advantages of the Internet would be that customers could use the same familiar computer network and technology for viewing and making changes in their accounts. In the mid-term, the Internet should also prove faster than the existing videotext system.
By estimates, the Internet has more than 200,000 users in Switzerland out of a total population of about seven million people. -- Zurich Newsroom, +41-1-631 7340
